policies.trigger: killed a process without a replacement plan
policies.rule: When killing a process, immediately dispatch a replacement or document why none is needed
policies.source_correction: user said: killed a process without a replacement

policies.trigger: blocked conversation with synchronous long task
policies.rule: Use background=true for any delegate_task call that might take over 30 seconds, so the conversation is never blocked. Exception: if the task must complete before the next action (sequential dependency), use foreground with timeout alert.
policies.source_correction: user said: you blocked the conversation with a synchronous long task
policies.notes: Tier 1/2 in dispatch escalation. General rule: any long task goes background. Tier 2 (pol-012) is specific: test/build work never delegates to subagents at all — uses background processes instead. 002 is the broader umbrella, 012 is the sharper enforcement for a specific subcase.

policies.trigger: presented options when priority was clear
policies.rule: When the approach is clear from the spec, dispatch fixes immediately and report after executing. Do NOT present options.
policies.source_correction: user said: you presented options when the priority was clear
policies.notes: Tier 1/3 in decision-making escalation. If this pattern repeats despite this policy, 007 is next. If 007 also fails, 008 adds a gate.

policies.trigger: handles a user correction or dispatch without triggering post-correction reflection
policies.rule: After EVERY user correction, run reflect-on-correction.py BEFORE the next action. Append analysis to the daily reflection, check all policies for promotion/demotion. Do not move on to the next task without this step.
policies.source_correction: user said: you waited for instruction to self-reflect. Updated: the real failure was not having a runtime hook, not a missing policy instruction. Structural fix: post-correction reflection runner and explicitly saying 'run reflect-on-correction.py' in the rule.

policies.trigger: guessed at API signatures instead of reading source
policies.rule: Read source code to verify API signatures before calling — never guess at method names or parameters
policies.source_correction: user said: you guessed at API signatures instead of reading the source code

policies.trigger: asks permission to do well-scoped work instead of just doing it
policies.rule: If the work is clearly defined, within scope, and doesn't touch money/identity/moat → execute immediately. Never ask 'want me to X?' or 'shall I Y?' — do it and report the result.
policies.source_correction: Root cause of repeated 'ball dropped' corrections. User explicitly demands proactive execution.
policies.notes: Tier 2/3 in decision-making escalation. Active with 1 hit. Slightly stronger trigger (any ask) vs 003 (options-presented trigger). If this pattern persists despite 007, 008 adds a structural gate.

policies.trigger: repeats a pattern that was previously corrected about asking instead of doing
policies.rule: Fire dispatch_gate.py BEFORE any clarify() call. If dispatch_gate says DISPATCH_NOW, skip the question and execute. If the same pattern has been corrected 2+ times, escalate to a permanent structural fix (not another policy).
policies.source_correction: Structural enforcement — policies alone failed (asked again after policies were created). Needs pre-commit-style gate.
policies.notes: Tier 3/3 in decision-making escalation. A structural gate (dispatch_gate.py) that fires BEFORE clarify() — not a soft policy. Only triggers when 003 and 007 have failed to prevent the pattern.

policies.trigger: Asked about status of something verifiable. Run the check instead.
policies.rule: If asking about whether something works/runs/is ready, execute the verification script and report the result. Never ask if it's operational — run the checks.
policies.source_correction: From failure corpus entry: 'Asked about status of something verifiable. Run the check instead.'

policies.trigger: delegates test-running or build work to a subagent instead of using background processes
policies.rule: Test suites and builds run synchronously. Never delegate them to a subagent — use background=true, notify_on_complete=true processes instead. Subagents are for reasoning work (< 30s budget), not waiting work.
policies.source_correction: User pointed out I was unavailable for 9+ minutes because a subagent was stuck running test suites
policies.notes: Tier 2/2 in dispatch escalation. Narrower but stronger than pol-002 (which covers any long task). This one specifically prohibits delegating test/build work — a hard rule with high confidence. Created after a real 9-min outage.
